newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open lower on Dow, dollar pressure.
newsitem.headline: German shares open lower on Dow, dollar pressure.

text.p: German shares backtracked somewhat on Tuesday after Wall Street closed lower overnight and the dollar continued weaker against the mark.

Dealers said the market was also pressured after Germany's six leading economic research institutes said a slight tightening in interest rates was possible if money supply growth stayed above target levels.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares, which had closed above the crucial 2,700 point mark on Monday, dropped 23.24 points, or 0.86 percent, to 2,680.09. Dealers said the market had lost momentum above 2,700 points, but still saw it consolidating.

Chemical company BASF AG moved against the market trend, adding to gains made on Monday after it announced a joint venture with Dutch firm DSM, even though DSM said it had made lower third quarter profits.
BASF gained 24 pfennigs to trade at 49.12 marks.
Meanwhile, car maker Volkswagen slipped back 5.25 marks to 592.50 as players took profits following gains made on Monday after the German government proposed repealing laws governing the carmaker.
For the rest of the week all eyes will be trained on the U.S. as a stream of data is released.
